title: 퉁구스카 대폭발

images.prompt: Siberian taiga at dawn, 1908, seen from high above: a vast forest where millions of trees lie flattened on the ground in a perfect radial pattern, every trunk pointing outward away from one center; in the very center a small cluster of tall bare branchless trunks still stands upright in low mist, catching a faint warm amber light. No crater, no hole. Pale empty dawn sky in the upper part.

Siberia, early morning of 30 June 1908: endless dark taiga forest under a pale sky that is split by one long, bright, glowing seam of light stretching across it like a crack, amber glow on the horizon, deep stillness, no buildings.

Siberian taiga, ground-level view: a seemingly endless sea of fallen tree trunks lying parallel on the ground, all their roots torn up on the same side, all pointing away from a far misty center on the horizon, grey dawn light, silent.

Siberian taiga: a flat, marshy, perfectly level bog clearing in the middle of a devastated forest, still water and moss, mist drifting low, absolutely no crater, no hole, no rock, no debris, nothing at all, eerie emptiness, grey light.

Siberian taiga: in the middle of a flattened forest, a group of tall upright tree trunks stripped of every branch and all bark, standing straight like telegraph poles over a misty bog, fallen trees lying all around them at a distance, a faint amber light, eerie silence.
